k: A reclusive businessman remaking Hell's Kitchen
st: Fisk unites the city's crime lords to remake Hell's Kitchen, until Daredevil and a witness put him in prison.
From his cell, Fisk takes control of the prison and uses Frank Castle to kill a rival inmate.
Fisk trades FBI help for his release and frames Daredevil, until Matt beats him and sends him back to prison.
As the Kingpin, Fisk runs the Tracksuit Mafia, until Kate beats him and Maya turns a gun on him.
Fisk survives Maya's shot and comes for her in Oklahoma, but she breaks his hold and he turns to politics.
Fisk is elected mayor of New York and seizes the city with his Anti-Vigilante Task Force.
Exposed at Karen's trial, Fisk resigns as mayor and takes a deal to leave New York without prosecution.

k: An art gallery owner who wins Fisk's heart
st: Vanessa learns what Fisk really is, chooses him anyway, and leaves the country as he falls.
Vanessa returns to marry Fisk and orders the murder of FBI Agent Ray Nadeem.
Vanessa runs Fisk's empire while he is away, and Matt learns she hired Bullseye to kill Foggy Nelson.
At Fisk's charity boxing match, a glass shard from Bullseye's attack strikes Vanessa's head, and she dies in hospital.

k: Fisk's loyal right-hand man
st: In the past, Wesley recruits Buck Cashman into Fisk's operation.
Wesley handles Fisk's deals and threats, keeping his boss's name out of sight.
Wesley abducts Karen Page to silence her, and she kills him with his own gun.

k: Fisk's accountant and money man
st: Owlsley manages the money behind Fisk's alliance and grows tired of his boss.
Owlsley plots against Fisk, who throws him down an elevator shaft.

k: A heroin queen with a mysterious past
st: Gao runs heroin through Fisk's alliance, then walks away as his empire falls.
Gao, still running heroin out of Chinatown, meets Daredevil face to face again.
Gao is revealed as a leader of the Hand moving heroin through Rand Enterprises, and Danny captures her.
Bakuto's people lock Gao in a cell at their compound, but she escapes.
As one of the Hand's Fingers, Gao is caught in the Midland Circle collapse.

k: A Japanese crime boss in Fisk's alliance
st: Nobu fights Daredevil for Fisk and dies engulfed in flames.
Nobu is back, alive, leading the Hand in Hell's Kitchen, and kills Elektra.
Matt throws Nobu off a rooftop.

k: A Russian mobster in Fisk's alliance
st: Anatoly interrupts Fisk's date with Vanessa, and Fisk kills him with a car door.

k: A Russian mobster in Fisk's alliance
st: Vladimir blames Daredevil for his brother's death, then learns Fisk was the killer.
Trapped by Fisk's corrupt police, Vladimir stays behind to hold them off and dies.

k: A detective on Fisk's payroll
st: Blake takes Fisk's money and ends up in hospital, where his partner Hoffman kills him.

k: A detective on Fisk's payroll
st: Hoffman kills his partner Blake on Fisk's orders, then flees for his life.
Hoffman turns himself in and testifies against Fisk.

k: A hitman working for Fisk
st: Healy kills a rival for Fisk, names his boss under Daredevil's fists, and then kills himself.

k: A small-time crook in Hell's Kitchen
st: Turk runs a human trafficking deal at the docks until Daredevil breaks it up.
Turk keeps selling guns in Hell's Kitchen and keeps running into Daredevil.
In Harlem, Turk tips off Tone to where Chico is hiding, which leads to the shooting at Pop's barbershop.
Diamondback hires Turk to sell his weapons on the street.
Turk is still hustling in Harlem as Luke hunts Bushmaster.

k: Fisk's fixer
st: Manning runs Fisk's plans outside prison and threatens Karen Page.
Daredevil dangles Manning off a roof until he agrees to testify, and Detective Mahoney arrests him.

k: An FBI chief in charge of Fisk's case
st: Hattley secretly works for Fisk inside the FBI, until the police raid on his hotel ends in her arrest.

k: An FBI agent with deadly aim and a broken mind
st: Fisk turns Agent Dex Poindexter into a killer who attacks the Bulletin in Daredevil's suit.
Dex turns on Fisk, who breaks his back, and after the police raid surgeons rebuild his spine.
Bullseye kills Foggy Nelson at Josie's, and Daredevil's fight with him ends in his arrest.
Bullseye escapes prison and shoots at Mayor Fisk, but Matt takes the bullet.
Bullseye saves Matt from the Task Force, then attacks Fisk's charity boxing match, fatally wounding Vanessa.
Bullseye fires at Fisk outside the courthouse and hits Buck, then flies off with Mr. Charles as his new operative.

k: Matt's old flame and a trained assassin
st: Elektra pulls Matt into her war with the Hand and dies taking Nobu's blade.
Revived by the Hand as the Black Sky, Elektra kills Alexandra and Stick and takes the Hand for herself.
Elektra stays with Matt as Midland Circle collapses on them both.

k: An ancient order of ninja
st: The Hand drains children's blood and digs a giant pit beneath Hell's Kitchen.
The Hand works inside Rand Enterprises and runs a dojo network through Bakuto.
The Defenders blow up Midland Circle, burying the Hand's leaders under the rubble.

k: Frank's former commanding officer
st: Colonel Schoonover, Frank's old commander, is the Blacksmith behind the shootout that killed Frank's family.
Frank hunts Schoonover down and kills him.

k: Boss of the Kitchen Irish
st: Finn Cooley captures Frank and tortures him, and Frank breaks free and kills him.

k: A small-time Kitchen Irish gangster
st: Grotto seeks Daredevil's protection, and Frank shoots him dead in front of Matt.

k: New York's District Attorney
st: Reyes hides her part in the botched sting that killed Frank's family, and is later shot dead.

k: A man whose words force people to obey
st: Kilgrave comes back for Jessica, forcing Hope Shlottman to kill her own parents.
Jessica lets Kilgrave think he controls her, then snaps his neck at the docks.
Kilgrave appears only in Jessica's mind, a memory she has to face.

k: An NYPD sergeant drawn into Jessica's war
st: Simpson takes combat pills from a secret program and hunts Jessica and Trish until Jessica knocks him out.
Simpson resurfaces with warnings about IGH and is killed soon after.

k: A super-strong killer tied to IGH
st: Alisa, Jessica's mother, kills people tied to IGH in fits of uncontrolled rage.
Alisa escapes prison and goes on the run with Jessica, until Trish shoots her dead.

k: The IGH doctor who gave Jessica her powers
st: Malus experiments on Trish to give her powers, then dies when his clinic blows up.

k: Jessica's best friend, a radio host
st: Trish takes Malus's procedure for powers and shoots Alisa dead.
With new powers and a mask, Trish kills criminals she has judged guilty.
Jessica stops Trish, who is sent to the Raft.

k: A genius serial killer who hates heroes
st: Sallinger hunts powered people he sees as cheats and kills Trish's mother Dorothy.
Jessica tricks Sallinger into confessing, and Trish kills him in police custody.

k: Harlem's nightclub-owning crime boss
st: Cornell Stokes runs guns out of Harlem's Paradise and starts a war with Luke Cage.
In a rage, his cousin Mariah beats Cornell to death.

k: A Harlem councilwoman with a crime family
st: Mariah kills her cousin Cottonmouth in a rage and pins the murder on Luke.
Mariah takes over Cornell's empire with Shades at her side and walks free.
As Black Mariah, she wars with Bushmaster and orders an attack on the Jamaican Stylers.
Jailed at last, Mariah is poisoned by her daughter Tilda and dies, leaving Harlem's Paradise to Luke.

k: A smooth enforcer with a long prison record
st: Shades, sent by Diamondback, steers Mariah toward taking Cornell's empire.
Shades kills his friend Comanche, then turns himself in and testifies against Mariah.

k: An arms dealer with a grudge against Luke
st: Willis Stryker, Luke's half-brother, hunts him with Judas bullets that can pierce his skin.
In a powered suit, Stryker loses to Luke in the street and is arrested.

k: A detective on Cottonmouth's payroll
st: Scarfe, Misty's corrupt partner, turns on Cottonmouth and is shot by him, later dying of the wound.

k: A nightshade-powered avenger from Jamaica
st: Bushmaster beats Luke and goes after Mariah's family to take back what Harlem stole from his.
Badly hurt, Bushmaster leaves New York for Jamaica.

k: A holistic doctor and Mariah's daughter
st: Tilda turns on her mother and poisons Mariah in prison.

k: Danny's father's partner, secretly alive
st: Harold, kept alive by the Hand, runs his children's lives from hiding.
Harold breaks from the Hand and turns on Danny, and his son Ward shoots him dead.

k: Colleen's sensei
st: Bakuto leads a faction of the Hand that wants Danny, until he is cut down and left for dead.
Bakuto returns alive, cuts off Misty Knight's arm, and is beheaded by Colleen.

k: Danny's brother in arms from K'un-Lun
st: Davos arrives from K'un-Lun, furious that Danny left his post.
With Joy's help, Davos steals the Iron Fist and attacks Chinatown's gangs.
Danny and Colleen defeat Davos, Colleen takes the Iron Fist, and the police take him away.

k: Ward's sister and a Rand executive
st: Joy helps Davos steal the Iron Fist, then breaks with him when his crusade turns deadly.

k: A former soldier with a second personality
st: Mary Walker is hired to watch Danny's allies, and her violent other self takes over.

k: The Hand's ancient, dying leader
st: Alexandra raises Elektra as the Black Sky to reach the treasure under Midland Circle.
Elektra turns on Alexandra and kills her.

k: A Finger of the Hand
st: Murakami fights the Defenders as the Hand digs under Midland Circle.
Murakami is caught in the Midland Circle collapse.

k: A Finger of the Hand
st: Captured by the Defenders, Sowande is killed by Stick, who sends his head to the Hand.

k: Frank's Marine friend, now a private army boss
st: Billy is revealed as Rawlins' partner, who knew about the hit on Frank's family.
Frank smashes Billy's face into a mirror at the carousel, leaving him scarred and under arrest.
Billy escapes the hospital with gaps in his memory and builds a crew of veterans.

k: A CIA officer with a past in Kandahar
st: Rawlins ran heroin through a covert unit and ordered the hit that killed Frank's family.
Frank kills Rawlins in a brutal fight at the carousel.

k: A young veteran unable to come home
st: Lewis starts a bombing campaign in New York and dies in his own blast.

k: A reformed zealot sent after a runaway girl
st: Pilgrim hunts Frank and Amy for the Schultzes, who hold his sons' safety over him.
Frank spares Pilgrim and sends him home to his sons.

k: A rich, devout couple guarding a secret
st: Anderson and Eliza Schultz send Pilgrim to silence Amy and protect their senator son.
Frank confronts the Schultzes at their home, and both of them die.

k: Billy Russo's therapist
st: Krista falls for her patient Billy and hides him from the law, until Madani throws her out a window.
Krista survives the fall, badly hurt.

k: Matriarch of the Gnucci crime family
st: Ma Gnucci puts a bounty on Frank Castle and sends Little Sicily's criminals after him.
Frank stops to protect bystanders instead of chasing her, and Ma Gnucci escapes.

k: A serial killer who paints with blood
st: Muse kills and drains his victims to paint murals across the city.
Muse is shot dead by his therapist, Heather Glenn.

k: Fisk's masked police unit
st: Mayor Fisk forms a task force of dirty cops to hunt vigilantes and seize the city.
The Task Force hunts Daredevil and locks down the courthouse during Karen's trial.

k: A dirty cop who copies the Punisher
st: Sergeant North, hiding behind a skull mask, guns down Hector Ayala.
North is caught in a grenade blast when the Task Force raids Matt's apartment.
North survives with burn scars, rejoins the Task Force, and refuses Powell's order to fire on protesters.

k: A dirty cop loyal to Fisk
st: Powell leads the dirty cops who become Fisk's Anti-Vigilante Task Force.
Powell orders his officers to fire on protesters at the courthouse, and North strikes him.

k: Fisk's fixer and enforcer
st: In the past, James Wesley recruits Buck into Fisk's operation.
Buck handles Fisk's dirty work as the new mayor takes power.
Buck shoots Daniel Blake dead for protecting BB Urich.
Buck takes a bullet Bullseye meant for Fisk outside the courthouse, and his fate is left unclear.

k: A gang of bros in matching tracksuits
st: The Tracksuits hunt Kate, believing she is the Ronin who wiped out their crew.
Kate and Clint beat the Tracksuits at Rockefeller Center, and police round them up.

k: Maya Lopez's second in command
st: Kazi takes orders from the Kingpin and is told to stop Maya.
Kazi refuses to walk away, and Maya kills him with an arrow.

k: The deaf leader of the Tracksuit Mafia
st: Maya hunts the Ronin who killed her father, then learns Fisk ordered his death.
Maya confronts Fisk with a gun as a shot rings out.
Back in Oklahoma, Maya defies Fisk, reconnects with her family, and breaks his hold on her.

k: Kate's mother, a security company CEO
st: Eleanor is secretly in business with Wilson Fisk.
Eleanor tries to cut ties with Fisk, and Kate sees her arrested.

k: A veteran S.H.I.E.L.D. agent
st: In season 1, Garrett is unmasked as the Clairvoyant, a HYDRA leader running Project Centipede.
Coulson destroys Garrett with an Asgardian weapon.

k: A S.H.I.E.L.D. specialist
st: In season 1, Ward is revealed as a HYDRA mole loyal to John Garrett.
Ward is caught by S.H.I.E.L.D. after Garrett falls.
In season 2, Ward escapes and leads his own war on S.H.I.E.L.D. with Kara Palamas.
In season 3, Coulson kills Ward on an alien planet.

k: An ancient Inhuman wearing Grant Ward's body
st: In season 3, Hive returns to Earth in Ward's body and bends Inhumans to his will.
Lincoln flies Hive into space, and both die in the blast.

k: A recruiter in a flower dress
st: In season 1, Raina recruits powered people for Centipede and HYDRA.
In season 2, Raina becomes a thorny Inhuman with visions and is killed by Jiaying.

k: A billionaire mining magnate
st: In season 1, Quinn builds a gravitonium machine and joins forces with Garrett.
A season 5 flashback shows Raina betraying Quinn, and the gravitonium swallows him.

k: A laid-off factory worker with sudden strength
st: In season 1, Garrett turns Mike into the cyborg Deathlok, using his son as leverage.
Mike turns on Garrett and walks away from HYDRA.

k: An Asgardian enchantress
st: In season 1, Lorelei escapes to Earth and enslaves men with her voice.
Sif takes Lorelei back to Asgard in chains.

k: A HYDRA scientist who never seems to age
st: In season 2, Whitehall leads HYDRA's hunt for the Obelisk.
Coulson shoots Whitehall dead before he can claim the Obelisk's power.

k: Whitehall's right-hand man
st: In season 2, Bakshi serves Whitehall and brainwashes HYDRA's prisoners.
S.H.I.E.L.D. captures Bakshi and hands him over to General Talbot.
Back with HYDRA, Bakshi dies leaping in front of a splinter bomb Simmons meant for Ward.

k: A S.H.I.E.L.D. agent brainwashed by HYDRA
st: In season 2, Kara wears a mask that copies faces and does HYDRA's work.
Kara joins Ward's war on S.H.I.E.L.D., and he kills her by mistake.

k: A man who takes on anything he touches
st: In season 2, Creel works for HYDRA until S.H.I.E.L.D. captures him.

k: Skye's volatile father, a doctor
st: In season 2, Cal seeks revenge on Whitehall and on S.H.I.E.L.D., which he blames for his wife's fate.
Cal kills Jiaying to save his daughter, and starts a new life with his memory erased.

k: Leader of a hidden Inhuman haven
st: In season 2, Jiaying, Skye's mother, leads the Inhumans of Afterlife.
Jiaying starts a war with S.H.I.E.L.D. and is killed by Cal.

k: An eyeless Inhuman who teleports
st: In season 2, Gordon serves Jiaying and carries Inhumans in and out of Afterlife.
In the season 2 finale, Gordon teleports behind Fitz and is impaled on the pipe in Fitz's hands.

k: A powerful businessman and HYDRA leader
st: In season 3, Malick brings Hive back to Earth to lead HYDRA.
Under Hive's influence, Daisy kills Malick.

k: Malick's Inhuman bodyguard
st: In season 3, Giyera moves objects with his mind and serves Malick and Hive.
Fitz kills Giyera with a cloaked gun aboard Hive's plane.

k: An Inhuman who charges objects with fire
st: In season 3, James joins Hive's cause.
In season 4, James returns as Hellfire, and Ghost Rider hands him over to S.H.I.E.L.D.

k: An anti-Inhuman hate group
st: The Watchdogs try to buy a HYDRA weapon from Colonel Ramon and test it on Yo-Yo.
The Watchdogs attack Inhumans across the country with Ivanov's money.

k: A Russian zealot who hates Inhumans
st: In season 4, Ivanov funds the Watchdogs and works with AIDA.
When his body is destroyed, Ivanov lives on as a head controlling android bodies.
In season 5, Ivanov returns with Hale's alliance, until Yo-Yo throws him out a window and he dies.

k: A US senator who fears Inhumans
st: In season 4, Senator Nadeer works with the Watchdogs against Inhumans.
Ivanov sends Tucker Shockley to test her with Terrigen, and Shockley turns Inhuman and explodes, killing Nadeer.

k: A corrupt Colombian police colonel
st: Ramon, the officer who killed Elena's cousin, tries to sell a HYDRA weapon to the Watchdogs.
When a Watchdog fires the weapon at Yo-Yo, its beam hits Ramon and kills him.

k: Robbie Reyes's uncle, a scientist
st: In season 4, Eli uses the Darkhold's science to make matter from nothing.
Ghost Rider drags Eli away through a portal.

k: A scientist obsessed with transhumanism
st: In season 4, Radcliffe builds AIDA and the Framework.
Radcliffe dies inside the Framework as it is erased.

k: An android assistant built by Radcliffe
st: In season 4, AIDA reads the Darkhold and traps the team in the Framework, ruling it as Madame Hydra.
AIDA becomes human as Ophelia, and Ghost Rider destroys her.

k: A Kree overseer of the last humans
st: In season 5, Kasius rules the humans of the Lighthouse in a ruined future.
Kasius loses his hold on the Lighthouse and dies fighting S.H.I.E.L.D.

k: Kasius's Kree enforcer
st: In season 5, Sinara enforces Kasius's rule with deadly flying spheres.
Sinara is killed in battle with S.H.I.E.L.D.

k: A US Air Force general
st: In season 5, Hale secretly works for HYDRA's remains and an alien alliance.
Hale's schemes collapse, and she is killed.

k: Hale's daughter, raised as a weapon
st: In season 5, Ruby, raised by HYDRA, cuts off Yo-Yo's arms.

k: An alliance of alien powers
st: In season 5, the Confederacy offers to protect Earth in return for Inhumans and gravitonium.

k: A US Air Force general who distrusts S.H.I.E.L.D.
st: In season 5, Talbot absorbs gravitonium and sets out to save Earth his own way.
Daisy fights Talbot and kills him.

k: An alien hunter wearing Coulson's face
st: In season 6, Sarge hunts the Shrikes across worlds and stabs May.
Sarge dies in the season 6 finale.

k: A body-hopping alien
st: In season 6, Izel jumps between bodies to open a gateway for her kind.

k: Androids from a fallen homeworld
st: In season 6, Chronicom Hunters come to Earth looking for a way to save their people.
In season 7, the Hunters chase S.H.I.E.L.D. through time to wipe it from history.
S.H.I.E.L.D. stops the Chronicom fleet in the final battle.

k: A Chronicom predictor
st: In season 7, Sibyl guides the Chronicom Hunters through time.
Sibyl is destroyed in the final battle.

k: Gideon Malick's brother
st: In season 7, Nathaniel joins the Chronicoms and gains Inhuman powers.
Nathaniel dies in the final battle.

k: A young Inhuman with a grudge
st: In season 7, Kora, Daisy's lost sister, joins Nathaniel Malick.
Kora breaks with Malick and fights at Daisy's side.

k: A Soviet spy ring
st: In season 1, Leviathan steals Howard Stark's deadliest inventions.
Peggy stops Leviathan's gas attack on New York and captures its leader, Fennhoff.

k: A Soviet psychiatrist
st: In season 1, Fennhoff hypnotizes Howard Stark to drop Midnight Oil gas on New York.
Peggy stops him, and he ends up in a cell next to Arnim Zola.

k: Peggy's friendly neighbor
st: In season 1, Dottie, a Leviathan assassin, befriends Peggy to spy on her.
In season 2, Dottie returns as a thief and spy, and she escapes after Peggy catches her.

k: A Hollywood star with a hidden genius
st: In season 2, Whitney absorbs Zero Matter and kills to gain power.
Peggy drains her of Zero Matter, and Whitney is locked in a mental hospital.

k: A Senate candidate in a secret council
st: In season 2, Chadwick covers up Zero Matter, until his wife Whitney kills him.

k: A Los Angeles mob boss
st: In season 2, Manfredi helps Whitney Frost, then helps Peggy stop her when Zero Matter consumes her.
Manfredi visits the broken Whitney in an asylum, still in love with her.

k: Black Bolt's brother, born without powers
st: Maximus seizes Attilan in a coup and sends the royal family fleeing to Earth.
Black Bolt seals Maximus in a vault as Attilan is abandoned.

k: Head of Attilan's Royal Guard
st: Auran, who can heal from any wound, hunts the royals on Earth for Maximus.
Auran comes back from a deadly blast and fights on for Maximus as the royals lead their people out of Attilan.

k: An Inhuman with destructive eyes
st: Mordis hunts the royal family on Earth and dies bringing a building down.

k: A scientist studying Inhumans
st: Declan works for Maximus and experiments on Black Bolt.
A revived, raging Gorgon throws Declan into a Terrigenesis chamber, killing him.

k: A group of wealthy Los Angeles parents
st: The parents of PRIDE secretly sacrifice teens for Jonah, until their own kids find out and run.
PRIDE join their children against the threats that come for their families.

k: A powerful man who funds PRIDE
st: Jonah needs PRIDE's sacrifices to live, and he kidnaps his daughter Karolina and others.
Nico stabs Jonah with the Staff of One, and he falls.
In a new body, Jonah traps Karolina and Chase, until Molly knocks him down and the Runaways trap him.

k: A sorceress from the Dark Dimension
st: Morgan le Fay lures Nico deeper into dark magic.
Tina's spell banishes Morgan back to the Dark Dimension.

k: A New Orleans police detective
st: Connors killed Tyrone's brother years ago and is still covering it up.
Tyrone absorbs Connors with his cloak and traps him in the Dark Dimension.
Back on Earth, Connors tries to make amends, until Tyrone's mother Adina shoots him dead.

k: A Roxxon executive
st: Scarborough tries to bury the truth about the Roxxon rig explosion that killed Tandy's father.
Tandy traps Scarborough in his own mind, leaving him in a coma.

k: A jazz musician with a dark gift
st: Andre runs a trafficking ring and feeds on people's despair to grow stronger.
Tandy and Tyrone defeat Andre in the finale.

k: A smooth operative with ties to Langley
st: Mr. Charles loses a weapons shipment to Fisk's Task Force and offers to help the governor push Fisk out.
Mr. Charles leaves New York on a plane, taking Bullseye on as his new operative.
